# Octree-based Hierarchy


## Overview
Octree-based Hierarchy is a family of hierarchical decomposition methods for volume rendering that organizes data into an octree structure to enable adaptive, multi-resolution rendering [S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like Pyramid-based LOD by using a 3D spatial subdivision (octree) rather than a 2D image-space pyramid or simple downsampling, allowing for precise culling of homogeneous 3D regions based on stored error metrics [S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The methods in this family share the mechanism of hierarchical decomposition and error-driven or distance-driven primitive selection, building on [Splatting](23-splatting.md).

1.  **Hierarchical Decomposition:** The input data (volume, point cloud, or Gaussian set) is organized into a tree structure (e.g., octree, pyramid, or sequential point tree) [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial][S6, unofficial]. Each node in the hierarchy represents a spatial region and stores aggregate properties (mean position, average color/density, total opacity, or merged covariance) derived from its children [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial].
2.  **Error Metric Computation:** For each internal node, a local error metric $E$ is computed to quantify the approximation cost of representing the node's children with the node's aggregate properties [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial]. Common metrics include the Root Mean Square (RMS) error of scalar values or the deviation of child positions/opacities from the parent's mean [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].
3.  **Adaptive Traversal and Selection:** During rendering, the hierarchy is traversed from the root to the leaves. A node is selected as a leaf (and thus rendered as a single primitive) if its error $E$ is below a user-defined threshold $\epsilon$ or if its projected screen-space footprint is smaller than a pixel threshold [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial]. If the error exceeds the threshold, the algorithm recurses to the children [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial].
4.  **Primitive Aggregation:** When a node is selected, its children are merged into a single representative primitive. The primitive's attributes (position, size, color, opacity) are computed as weighted averages or sums of the children's attributes [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial]. For Gaussian splats, this involves merging covariances and spherical harmonics coefficients [S3, unofficial].
5.  **Multi-Resolution Rendering:** The final image is composed of primitives from various levels of the hierarchy, allowing for efficient culling of distant or homogeneous regions while maintaining fidelity in foreground or complex areas [S1, S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial][S6, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Octree-based Splatting](8067-octree-based-splatting.md)
Octree-based Splatting is an object-order interactive volume rendering technique that approximates volume contributions using an octree representation to balance rendering speed and image quality. It sets itself apart from standard splatting by dynamically adjusting the size of geometric primitives based on the hierarchical structure of the data, allowing larger regions to be rendered with fewer primitives when the visual error is within a specified tolerance. This method builds on [Octree-based Hierarchy](12129-octree-based-hierarchy.md) by utilizing the stored error metrics to prune the traversal depth during the rendering pass.

### Hierarchical Splat Culling
Splats are culled prior to sorting and rendering using a custom octree to optimize performance [S1, unofficial].

### Splatting-Based AMR Volume Rendering
A volume rendering technique using kD-tree and octree-based domain subdivision to specify isovalue ranges and transfer functions, rendering via hierarchical splatting [S2, unofficial].
1. Subdivide the domain using kD-tree and octree structures [S2, unofficial].
2. Specify isovalue range and transfer function [S2, unofficial].
3. Render using hierarchical splatting [S2, unofficial].

### Octree Splatting
1. Approximate non-leaf octree nodes by kernels with a radius twice the radius of the children's kernels, creating a magnified footprint [S3, unofficial].
2. Store the children's average and an error metric based on standard deviation in each parent node, using a pre-set error to select nodes during rendering [S3, unofficial].

## Background
The use of octrees in volume rendering dates back to the early 1990s. Laur and Hanrahan proposed an implementation that approximates non-leaf octree nodes by kernels with a magnified footprint, storing error metrics based on standard deviation to guide rendering [S3, unofficial]. In the context of Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR), Park et al. (2002) introduced splatting-based volume rendering using kD-tree and octree-based domain subdivision to specify isovalue ranges and transfer functions [S2, unofficial]. More recently, the technique has been adapted for 3D Gaussian Splatting, where custom octrees are used to cull splats prior to sorting and rendering to optimize performance in real-time viewers [S1, unofficial].
